newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps - mogas grabs centre stage, again.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps - mogas grabs centre stage, again.

text.p: Gasoline regained centre-stage of the European oil swaps market on Wednesday.
Dealers said gasoline swpas were $3 or so stronger on bullish API data, firm NYMEX prices and the tight supply situation in NWE.
Brent crude CFDs were essentially unchanged while naphtha was 75 cents to $1 higher, in part because of gasoline's strength.
Fuel oil was $1 or so stronger, but very quiet.
Gasoline saw August swaps trade at $203.00 up from $199.25 seen on Tuesday with September tracking higher to $195.00.
Brent CFDs were unchanged with the balance of this week at +12 cents against September with Augsut 4-8 at + 1 cent, up very narrowly from flat against September on Tuesday.
August 11-15 was pegged at -4/5 cents cents from -5 cents with Augsut 18-22 put at -7 cents from -8 cents.
Gas oil crack spreads saw 4Q at $4.40, 1Q at $4.45 and 2Q at $3.95.
Naphtha swaps received a small boost from gasoline's strength with August moving 75 cents to $1 up to $191.25 with September remaining backwardated at $188.00.
